correctness.rationale: All n>=4 lie in a unique dyadic block. The proposed low and high position sets meet each zero-only, exactly-one-one, and multiple-one factor by explicit occurrence choices. A projection lemma moves suffix-selected positions to a distinguished zero of the preceding complete gap, proving gamma(W_m 0^h)>=gamma(W_m). Uniquely occurring consecutive-one-gap factors, a near-last-one factor, and a final long zero-run factor occupy pairwise disjoint required regions and give exact matching lower bounds, with m=2 and n<=3 treated separately. The standalone standard-library verifier passed complete factor-coverage checks through 184 and at selected larger lengths up to 512, checked every lower certificate region, and exhaustively minimized n<=14. Finite tests do not replace the symbolic argument.

originality.rationale: The most directly relevant source, Schaeffer and Shallit arXiv:2012.06840 Section 6 Theorem 8, proves upper bounds with the identical underlying object, indices up to a shift, powers-of-four length regimes, and values. Its accompanying text expressly leaves the matching lower bound to other techniques. The present exact theorem adds that missing lower bound at every length. Restivo et al. arXiv:2206.00376 Example 3 supplies only Theta(log n) for this sequence, and the related works on other words do not imply the fine-grained profile. Published-record searches for equivalent or stronger results found no decisive covering result, though absence of search hits cannot establish publication priority.
residual_risks: Unindexed, unpublished, or differently titled sharp lower bounds might exist; searched abstracts and publication records cannot prove uniqueness of research priority.
Some related nonidentical-word papers were inspected at their definitions and main statements rather than every appendix; no decisive same-word comparison was left unresolved.
A full independent proof audit has not been performed.

value.rationale: The exact minimum-cardinality profile of a canonical sparse automatic word was naturally singled out by prior explicit but nonsharp upper constructions. The theorem supplies matching all-length lower bounds, rigorously settles every jump threshold at 6 times a power of four, and gives a structural projection lemma plus disjoint occurrence certificates. It strengthens the previous asymptotic classification and resolves a mathematically motivated sharpness question rather than only computing examples.
